title: PlatformIdentity is harvestable from the public Attestor API and re-wrappable onto any candidate
description:
Confirmed empirically by a verification agent with a throwaway crate depending on persona-attestors by path.

The struct literal is correctly refused (E0451, asked_at is private). But PlatformIdentity is pub, re-exported at lib.rs:16, and Clone. A downstream crate calls UnixAttestor::prove(), owns the returned Vec<Evidence>, destructures out the PlatformIdentity, and re-wraps it around an arbitrary Candidate:

  Claim::derive(&Candidate::new("unix", SshLocal, "unix/0", "root"), b"a-challenge-we-never-answered", &[Evidence::PlatformAssertion(p)])
  -> Some(source=unix assurance=Iaa1 presence=None id=spiffe://ssh.local/unix/0 name=root)

Two gaps combine: binds_to() (claim.rs:416) returns true unconditionally for this variant, and Claim::derive never checks evidence corresponds to the candidate. Every other variant is either unconstructable (VerifiedToken, HardwareTouch have no constructor at all) or challenge-bound (Possession). This is the first with neither.

Root cause is a deliberate simplification: the implementer left the uid OUT of PlatformIdentity ('would be never-read, dead_code fires'). That omission is exactly what removes the binding.

Blast radius is the library type guarantee, not personad itself -- the daemon builds claims from its own attestors. But that guarantee is the entire point of the okek refactor.
